what_this_is: The between-arm contrast with the instrument held fixed: both arms judged under the shipped codebook, the same pinned model, the same adjudicator prompt and the same batch size. The confounded contrast the paper first reported is printed beside it.
why_newcombe: An interval for the DIFFERENCE, not two intervals that happen to overlap. Built from Wilson intervals so it behaves where responsiveness lives, near 0.02.

model_id_witnessed.stated_where: My system prompt states: "You are powered by the model named Opus 5. The exact model ID is claude-opus-5."

codebook_source: judging/*_prompt_v1.txt, extracted byte-for-byte from the SHIPPED scripts

PRIMARY_matched_contrast_paired_question.method: percentile paired-question cluster bootstrap; clusters are the 134 questions, both arms resampled on the same draw, all claims of a question move together
PRIMARY_matched_contrast_paired_question.conditional_on: the observed labels and the one captured generation per arm; the question set is authored, not a probability sample, so this is not a statement about representativeness, judge error or generation variance

entailment.why_not_newcombe: Newcombe's hybrid score is for two INDEPENDENT binomial proportions. Both arms answer the same 134 questions (paired) and claims are nested in questions (clustered), so neither assumption holds. It is retained below to show what the wrong assumption costs.

matched_contrast.method: Newcombe hybrid score (square-and-add) on Wilson intervals

confounded_contrast_as_first_reported.method: Newcombe hybrid score (square-and-add) on Wilson intervals
